notes: An update no longer freezes pactum

entries.title: An update no longer freezes pactum
entries.detail: When pactum installed an update, it could stop at "Installing". Then About, Docs and Quit did nothing, while the page still worked. Now pactum quits within 3 seconds, and the update goes on.

entries.title: pactum trusts only its own server
entries.detail: pactum shows only pages from the server it started itself. Before, another program on this Mac that took pactum's port first could have shown its pages in pactum's window. Now pactum shows why instead, and opens nothing in the browser.

entries.title: Safer and faster
entries.detail: pactum starts faster: it reads your files in about half the time. Its server keeps running after a bad request, and a save that fails now says "not saved" instead of stopping pactum. It is built with Node's newest security fixes.

entries.title: A Minimum Viable Efficiency for each efficiency KPI
entries.detail: Data ISGs has a Minimum Viable Efficiency for each of the six efficiency KPIs, with the same selectors as the Minimum Viable Maturity. Your one value became each KPI's. Each efficiency spider draws them in amber, with the name under that spider; the Minimum Viable Maturity's name stands under the maturity spider. The 2×2 draws their mean. A switch Minimum Viable Efficiency, left of Minimum Viable Maturity, shows or hides it.

entries.title: A softer amber for the selected ISG
entries.detail: The amber behind the selected ISG's row, its figures and its spiders is softer, and so is the amber area in its spiders, like the cross-hatch in the 2×2.

entries.title: Both minimums at the top of Data ISGs
entries.detail: Data ISGs starts with Minimum Viable: the Minimum Viable Efficiency, then the Minimum Viable Maturity, in a section of their own. The cross-hatch in the 2×2 is softer. Docs, the Field Manual, names today's pages and says your data is in iCloud.

entries.title: Minimum Viable Maturity and Minimum Viable Efficiency
entries.detail: The Minimum Viable Standard is now called Minimum Viable Maturity. Data ISGs has a new part, Efficiency ISGs: enter the Minimum Viable Efficiency, 0 to 5. The 2×2 draws it as an amber line up the chart, and cross-hatches the corner where an ISG meets both minimums. Docs, the Field Manual, says so too.

entries.title: Minimum Viable Standard
entries.detail: The Accepted Minimum is now called Minimum Viable Standard: on the switch, in the legends of the spiders and the 2×2, and in the table under Data ISGs. Your values stay as they were.

entries.title: Accepted Minimum in the 2×2, whole names on the buttons
entries.detail: The 2×2 draws the Accepted Minimum as an amber line at the mean of its levels, as in the spiders, with a legend under it. The ISG buttons show whole names, such as ID ISG D-BAUG and ISG D-ARCH. The note under the overview no longer points to the KPIs without data.

entries.title: Arrows on every column
entries.detail: Every column title in the overview shows two small arrows, so you see that it sorts. A sorted title keeps only one: up when the lowest is first, down when the highest is first.

entries.title: Sort the overview
entries.detail: Click a column's title in the overview to sort all ISGs by it, the best first. Click again to turn the order round, and a third time to go back. The table is one list now, without the rows "ID ISGs" and "Departmental ISGs"; without a click, the order is as before.

entries.title: No hover left behind
entries.detail: A scroll now closes every hover. Before, a hover of the 2×2 could stay on the page after a scroll with the trackpad, far from its bubble.

entries.title: Calm hovers
entries.detail: Every hover now looks the same: the ISG, what is shown, one value, then labels and numbers in straight columns and a short note, in one size of text. The spiders' hover shows the KPIs and the nine levels as two small tables.

entries.title: Nothing typed is lost when pactum quits, and a clear hover
entries.detail: Before pactum quits, for an update too, it saves what you are typing under Data ISGs. In the overview, the hover shows the ISG, the KPI under it, the value, and then the median, the standing and the two figures behind it in two straight columns, without file names.

entries.title: Bigger spiders, cleaner figures and names
entries.detail: The spiders are bigger and use the card's room, with the legend beside them. The specifics stay in the figures, not between the spiders. The figures show names and numbers only; point at a row to see its file. In the 2×2, every name sits right beside its bubble: names are measured, not guessed, so ID ISG D-BIOL no longer goes a line up.

entries.title: Whole specifics, readable names
entries.detail: Under Specifics ISGs, each field is as tall as its text, so long points are no longer cut off. In the 2×2, a picked ISG's name stays where it was, so it no longer lies on a neighbour's name (ISG D-INFK and ISG D-HEST).

entries.title: Copy one ISG as a picture
entries.detail: In an ISG's view of its own, Copy picture puts its row, the 2×2 with its figures, and its spiders on the clipboard, sharp at twice the size, ready to paste. The amber of a selection is softer. The spiders' hover keeps each line on one line. The search is gone from the top bar. The second page is now called Data ISGs, with the titles Maturity ISGs and Specifics ISGs.

entries.title: The whole 2×2 for a group too
entries.detail: With ID ISGs or Departmental ISGs on, the efficiency and maturity chart still shows all ISGs, where they stand among all. The table and the spiders show the group.

entries.title: One ISG at a glance, and its specifics
entries.detail: Buttons replace the group menu: All ISGs, ID ISGs, Departmental ISGs, and one button per ISG. An ISG's button shows that ISG alone: its row, the 2×2 of all ISGs with its figures, its spiders. Maturity ISGs has a section Specifics: a few points per ISG, shown between its spiders and in its figures. The KPI numbers are the ones in the sheet KPIs ID ISGs. A spider's hover names each KPI in full, Maturity Ø ID and ISG take one line each, and an ID ISG's own maturity is ID's.

entries.title: The pages as icons beside Settings, and the workbook's new rows
entries.detail: KPIs ISGs and Maturity ISGs are now icon buttons at the top right, left of Settings, in folia's style: amber when on. pactum reads the workbook's new rows, staff per FTE with and without workplace, with their Average ID CxS, and checks its own numbers against them. Where they differ, Settings › Data names the cells.

entries.title: More room: the pages on top, Data in Settings
entries.detail: The sidebar is gone. KPIs ISGs and Maturity ISGs are buttons at the top, so the pages have the whole width. Data is now in Settings. The overview has no column Heads; staff per FTE comes in two columns, with workplace and without workplace; and every column title takes two lines at most. The line about the Average ID CxS under the profiles is gone.

entries.title: The KPI page ends with the profiles
entries.detail: The section Development is gone from the KPI comparison. It only said that the trend begins with the second year.

entries.title: Data sources on the Data page, and a new title
entries.detail: The KPI catalog moved from under the profiles to the Data page. It is its own section there, Data sources: every KPI, where it comes from, and whether it has data. The search takes a KPI there. The KPI page is now called KPI comparison of ETH IT Service Groups.

entries.title: Your files are in iCloud Drive
entries.detail: pactum reads its files from iCloud Drive › Armarium › pactum › Input, so your other Mac has them too. Settings › About pactum says so under Where your data lives.

entries.title: The Field Manual has the updated rubric
entries.detail: Docs opens the Field Manual with the maturity rubric as it was sent to the ISGs: the strict requirements of each level, Accepted Minimum at Defined and Gold Standard at Optimised. It also names the two tables of Enter maturity.

entries.title: The ISG teams' table holds the departmental ISGs
entries.detail: The table filled by the ISG teams lists the departmental ISGs only. Under each maturity spider, Maturity Ø ISG stands to the right of Maturity Ø ID, and the legend says Maturity by the ID in place of Own profile.

entries.title: Figures beside the table on the big screen
entries.detail: In a window of 1720 px the figures went under the overview. The two maturity headers now take two lines, so the table is narrower and the figures stand beside it again.

entries.title: The ISG teams' own maturity
entries.detail: Enter maturity has a second table, filled by the ISG teams: the same nine levels, for themselves. The first table is the one ID fills. The overview shows Maturity Ø ID and Maturity Ø ISG, and each maturity spider draws the ISG team's levels as a second line. Target is now Accepted Minimum, Research is Research/Business, and the complexity factor is off when the page opens.

entries.title: A picked spider goes first, and the table has no gaps
entries.detail: A spider you click goes to the top of the profiles, as one picked in the table or the 2×2, and it stays under your mouse: the page moves with it. The overview has no gaps between its cells any more, so a row is one band and the amber edge of the selected row runs unbroken.

entries.title: The selected row in amber
entries.detail: The selected ISG's row in the overview has the same amber ground and amber edge as its figures and its spiders. Its KPI cells keep their grey steps on the amber, so the standing still shows.

entries.title: The figures turn amber with the selection
entries.detail: When you select an ISG, the figures beside the table turn amber, as its row, its bubble and its spiders do.

entries.title: The page stays where you are
entries.detail: Picking an ISG in the table, the 2×2 or the profiles no longer moves the page; only the search goes to its row. A profile you click stays in its place. Each profile's legend stands beside its spiders. The complexity factor is on from the start. The figures no longer show the total cost. The overview's groups read ID ISGs and Departmental ISGs.

entries.title: The figures name the factor's file
entries.detail: Under the complexity factor, the figures no longer say who set it. They name where it is saved, as for every other figure: Input/pactum-eingaben.json.

entries.title: A quieter 2×2, no column Set by, more in the figures
entries.detail: The efficiency and maturity chart no longer shows values under the mouse. Enter maturity has no column Set by any more: a factor you enter counts as set by ID. The figures of an ISG add its devices on ID Client Delivery platforms, and the tickets are named as what they are: tickets solved by ID Service Desk.

entries.title: Figures beside the table, a legend on every profile
entries.detail: The figures of the selected ISG stand to the right of the overview, always, so nothing jumps in when you pick a row. The column of KPIs without data is gone; they are in the KPI catalog. Every profile has its own legend, and the selected ISG's profile comes first. In the 2×2, the mouse shows its efficiency and maturity on the axes, and a bubble from fewer KPIs is a dashed ring. A complexity factor of 1 shows as 1.0, and Enter goes to the next factor.

entries.title: One number for efficiency, one for maturity
entries.detail: Each ISG has two single numbers for comparison. Efficiency Ø is the mean standing, 0 to 5, in the efficiency KPIs: it compares with the ISGs shown. Maturity Ø is the mean level entered, 1 to 5. Both end each row of the table and stand under the spiders on each card. When not all parts are in, the number says how many are, as in "2 of 9".

entries.title: Settings… in About pactum
entries.detail: The About pactum window has a Settings… button, as folia's has. It opens pactum and its Settings.

entries.title: Whole names in the 2×2
entries.detail: In the efficiency and maturity chart, every bubble carries its whole name: ID ISG D-BAUG for an ID ISG, ISG D-BSSE for a departmental one.

entries.title: Docs opens the pactum Field Manual
entries.detail: About pactum › Docs and Settings › About pactum › Docs open the Field Manual: what pactum is, and the maturity rubric with its five levels for each of the nine dimensions. In the Mac app it opens in a window of its own, also without the internet.

entries.title: Not rated has its own strip
entries.detail: In the efficiency and maturity chart, an ISG without a maturity no longer sits at level 3 as if rated. It stands in a strip "Not rated" under the chart, at its efficiency.
